discussion_comments.comment_body: Can you name this something else?  Sets already have a `discard` method with a completely different meaning. No need to create confusion by giving this the same name.

Oh, it's unfortunate that `PyFrozenSetWriter_Discard()` name is close `set.discard()`, but has a different meaning (discard the temporary frozenset and destroy the writer) :-(

If possible, I would prefer to reuse Create/Finish/Discard names, since they are already used by 3 other "Writer" C API:

* [PyUnicodeWriter](https://docs.python.org/dev/c-api/unicode.html#pyunicodewriter)
* [PyBytesWriter](https://docs.python.org/dev/c-api/bytes.html#pybyteswriter)
* [PyLongWriter](https://docs.python.org/dev/c-api/long.html#pylongwriter-api)

For now, I only propose functions to add items to the writer. If someone needs "more complex" use cases, I would suggest creating a mutable set, and then convert it to a frozenset (call `PyFrozenNew_New(temp_set)`).

If later a discard method is added, it can be called `PyFrozenSetWriter_DiscardItem(writer, item)`.
Move macros definition to the function. And undef it in the end.
And I think we should use name like `set_modified`.

This comment / function name are low on context. The function name doesn't suggest that this has anything to do with comprehensions, but the comment assumes the reader knows that it does, and knows what a "compressed delta" is.

In general it would be really nice to have somewhere in a comment a more comprehensive explanation of how comprehension inlining is intended to work. (Yes, that would have been good in the previous version too!)
